On our dataset of fingertip forces recorded with tactile sensors, HOForce reduces normal-force MAE by 24.5% relative to the strongest baseline. The recovered forces reproduce object motion in MuJoCo and transfer to other engines after adaptation.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Ying Wei, Defu Lian
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper examines how on-policy distillation alters ReAct interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and detrimental effects on performance.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zhaolu Wang, Jiacheng Xu, Lihong Wang, Shuqing Wang, Jianjie Fang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: HandWorldBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating hand-centric world models, highlighting the disparity between hand-pose control and effective object-state persistence across various embodiments.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, we introduce HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. To construct the benchmark, we develop a data curation pipeline that extracts hand-object interaction clips and screens them for quality, yielding 20,500 high-quality egocentric clips from over 600 hours of footage. We then manually select 500 clips covering seven task families for evaluation. Benchmarking eleven models under a unified protocol reveals that stronger hand-pose control does not consistently translate into coherent object-state evolution and persistence or robust cross-embodiment performance, with several specialized hand-control models underperforming general-purpose text/image-to-video generators on dexterous-hand tasks.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zihe Huang, Sirui Zhou, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Teng Ma
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The F$^3$ framework enhances world-action models by optimizing experience utilization through Form, Fit, and Fusion, achieving significant performance improvements in robotic tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. What, then, makes good experience for a WAM? We show that experience is valuable only in use: its value depends not on whether the source rollout succeeded but on what is stored, when it is used, and where it enters the policy. We therefore propose F$^3$, which makes these three decisions with Form, Fit, and Fusion. Form compresses successful and failed rollouts alike into short, verified operation records; Fit teaches the policy to read a record and to predict when it helps; Fusion injects the record's images, text and actions into the policy as a prefix and an action prior. Trained once on only 200 examples and deployed with a growing experience library, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on MolmoSpaces and RoboLab without any training on RoboLab: over native Cosmos 3 Nano, it raises success by 12.0 pp and 10.8 pp, reduces steps to success by 12.2% and 11.3%, and cuts regressions by 57%.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Rong Zou, Haiqing Hao, Davide Scaramuzza
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: ALIVE is an event-based method that efficiently updates visual foundation model features using events, significantly improving performance and reducing computational costs across various tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Rethinking Event-Based Object Detection through Representation-Level Temporal Aggregation and Model-Level Hypergraph Reasoning
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Meisen Wang, Hao Deng, Wei Bao, Chengjie Wang, Zhiqiang Tian
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper introduces Ev-DTAD, an event-based object detection framework that enhances accuracy through hierarchical temporal aggregation and hypergraph reasoning, addressing limitations in existing methods.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Event cameras provide microsecond-level temporal resolution, low latency, and high dynamic range, offering potential for perception under fast motion and challenging illumination conditions. However, existing Event-based Object Detection (EOD) methods face limitations at both the representation and model levels: prior event representations usually encode temporal information indirectly through redundant structures, while detection models struggle to explicitly aggregate fragmented event responses into coherent high-order object features. To address these limitations, we present \textbf{Event Dual Temporal-Relational Aggregation Detector (Ev-DTAD)}, a unified EOD framework that integrates representation-level temporal encoding with model-level temporal-hypergraph reasoning. Specifically, we introduce \textbf{Hierarchical Temporal Aggregation (HTA)}, a compact three-channel pseudo-RGB representation that explicitly embeds temporal information across intra- and inter-window events. To further enhance detection under sparse and fragmented event responses, we propose \textbf{Frequency-aware Hypergraph Temporal Fusion (FHTF)}, which refines multi-scale event features through temporal evolution modeling and high-order relational reasoning. Extensive experiments on Gen1 (\textbf{+0.8 mAP}), 1Mpx/Gen4 (\textbf{+0.5 mAP}), and eTraM (\textbf{+3.0 mAP}) demonstrate that Ev-DTAD achieves a competitive accuracy--efficiency trade-off, validating the complementarity between compact temporal representation and temporal-hypergraph feature reasoning (Fig.~\ref{fig:bubble}). The code is available at: https://github.com/meisenwang/Ev-DTAD.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: Phoenix introduces a novel scene structure representation for world-action models, enhancing manipulation performance through dual-teacher distillation and causal aggregation of visual features.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Read Together, Answer Apart: How Earlier Questions Help Vision-Language Models Look
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xinyi Guo, Kaile Huang, Xitong Ling, Mingyi He, Chende Zheng
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The study reveals that co-asking enhances vision-language model accuracy by leveraging earlier questions to improve attention, while introducing a decoding mask further boosts performance.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are often asked several questions about the same image in a single prompt (co-asking), yet existing evaluations report conflicting accuracy gains and hallucinations at the prompt level without tracking how individual answers change. By pairing each question's single-question and co-asked answers across 22 open-weight VLMs (1B-35B), we find that erratic net shifts reflect two opposing effects: on Densely Captioned Images (DCI), every model repairs 15.4%-29.8% of its single-question errors under co-asking, while the share of correct answers turned wrong falls from 30.8% on weaker models to 4.7% on stronger ones. Across all 14 models supporting custom attention masks, we show through attention readouts and layer-window interventions that earlier same-image questions read visual information into their question tokens in the early-to-middle layers during prefill, helping later questions concentrate image attention onto their queried targets. This visual help accumulates across the scene even across non-overlapping regions, whereas blocking earlier questions from attending to the image lowers both target localization and accuracy in all 14 models. While cross-question help is established during shared question reading, part of the co-asking damage enters later during answer decoding when the decoder attends to other question stems. We therefore introduce Read Together, Answer Apart, a training-free decoding mask that keeps shared prefill intact and isolates each answer from other stems, improving co-asking accuracy on 12 of 14 models on DCI (up to +4.71 percentage points, closing 70% of the pooled gap to asking alone) and on 10, 8, and 5 of the 14 models on WebUI, FinTabNet, and GQA (up to +11.4, +5.3, and +1.1 points).

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Shiwei Wu, Yuwen Pan, Zhi Li, Yaowen Li, Yan Zhou
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: AeroRSI is a framework that enables UAVs to iteratively learn from their navigation failures, improving success rates and reducing collisions without additional human input.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Jiarui Guo, Saining Zhang, Jiaying Wan, Jiawei Weng, Junhao Chen
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: RFW-S is a comprehensive dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified deformable objects, enhancing robotic simulation with reliable physical properties and interaction behaviors across diverse categories.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper proposes a wire protocol for detecting silent faults at the environment-trainer boundary in reinforcement learning, demonstrating effective fault identification through step ledgers and episode records.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: EmbodiedLab: Beyond Manipulation, Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Hongcheng Gao, Zelin Zheng, Alex Zhou, Jay Zhu, Shijia Ge
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: EmbodiedLab introduces a simulated laboratory for benchmarking embodied agents that must physically act to discover hidden properties, enhancing understanding through 35 quantitative experiments.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Physical action not only changes the state of an environment but is also the way to know its hidden properties: what cannot be seen must be inferred from the feedback to the change. As embodied agents advance from executing procedures to pursuing goals, success depends on properties neither given nor visible, so they must act to know. Existing benchmarks separate changing from knowing: manipulation benchmarks give the target state, so nothing has to be found out, whereas exploration and discovery benchmarks let the agent find out by looking or querying, so nothing physical has to be changed. Quantitative science experiments offer a natural testbed: the properties sought are new in every instance, appear only in instrument readings under conditions the agent sets up, and can be checked exactly. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a simulated laboratory of 35 such experiments. Given only a goal, the agent must decide what to measure, operate the apparatus with a robot arm, read instruments through cameras and judge when its readings suffice. Its 30 determination tasks specify what to find out, whereas its 5 optimization tasks ask only for the best result the apparatus allows. With native control, the strongest of seven frontier agents succeeds on 41.4% of the tasks. Ablations reveal two bottlenecks: contact-rich manipulation, where ground-truth depth and motion planning change the success rate by at most 10 points, whereas executing every operation for the agent on five of the tasks raises it from at most 20% to at least 70%, so what an agent can know is bounded by how reliably it acts; and closed-loop experimental rigor, where with manipulation supplied, agents fail to gather sufficient readings or read instruments accurately, and most optimization runs stop at one design. Beyond evaluation, EmbodiedLab offers a resamplable environment with verifiable rewards for training embodied agents.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Autonomous Video Generation for Self-Evolving World Models
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xin Wang, Wenxuan Liu, Tongtong Feng, Wenwu Zhu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: This paper introduces autonomous video generation for self-evolving world models, emphasizing counterfactual controllability and closed-loop optimization to enhance actionable predictions for embodied agents.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Large-scale video generation models are increasingly described as world models because they can learn rich spatiotemporal regularities from visual data. We argue that an ideal world model should benefit in a self-evolving generative character. As such, a self-evolving world model can be realized via a generative model conditioned by various constraints, whose future predictions are refined through feedback. However, traditional visually plausible predictions alone are not enough to establish whether an imagined future is physically actionable for a particular embodied agent, failing to provide informative feedback from environments for self-evolving improvement. To realize self-evolving world models, this article proposes the concept of autonomous video generation, which is evaluated through counterfactual controllability, i.e., the ability to i) generate intervention-conditioned futures, ii) bind these future frames to embodiment constraints, iii) verify them under distribution shifts, and iv) distil surviving branches into compact variables for decision-making. We formalize a four-stage closed-loop optimization of Generation, Binding, Verification and Distillation, together with four corresponding evaluation metrics: novelty, consistency, out-of-distribution (OOD) and efficiency. We further discuss two examples, i.e., drones and manipulators, as early embodied testbeds where wind, sensing limits, actuation delay, contact dynamics and recovery constraints can be systematically perturbed and verified. The central claim is that the framework of autonomous video generation for self-evolving world models should not be judged by video fidelity alone, but by whether the generated frames improve valid action under counterfactual interventions and various embodiment constraints.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: DLWM: Diverse Latent World Models for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: DLWM introduces a multimodal reasoning framework that utilizes diverse latent hypotheses and adaptive reinforcement learning to enhance accuracy and reduce memory usage in complex reasoning tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have improved considerably in recent years. Existing approaches typically rely on explicit chain-of-thought or continuous latent-space trajectories to enhance multi-step reasoning. However, these methods generally assume that an input admits a single latent interpretation and unfold reasoning along a fixed path or under a uniform computation budget. In real-world multimodal settings, visual observations are often subject to occlusion, blur, viewpoint variation, or semantic ambiguity, giving rise to multiple plausible interpretations. A uniform reasoning strategy not only limits the model's ability to explore multiple hypotheses but also incurs high memory usage and rollout cost. We present DLWM (Diverse Latent World Models), a multimodal reasoning framework that combines latent-space reasoning with reinforcement learning. First, we construct a set of diverse latent world hypotheses in continuous latent space, each representing a candidate interpretation of the visual input, and unfold latent reasoning independently on each hypothesis. An orthogonality-based diversity regularizer discourages hypothesis collapse. Second, we formulate the latent reasoning process as a resource-constrained sequential decision problem and introduce a resource-aware reinforcement learning policy that adaptively allocates computation across hypotheses, dynamically deciding whether to expand a reasoning path, prune a hypothesis, merge reasoning paths, or produce the final answer, thereby substantially reducing memory footprint and improving rollout efficiency. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DLWM outperforms existing methods by 2-5 points in accuracy while reducing memory usage by 24%.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xianhao Pan, Chi Li, Hanchao Li, Yunxin Liu, Jiankai Sun
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: JEPA Dots introduces a dual-latent framework for language-guided robot control, achieving 84.9% success by separating dynamics and task representations while maintaining invariant world predictions.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Predictive world models for language-guided robot control face a fundamental conditioning challenge: instructions should influence action selection without altering the predicted consequences of fixed actions under identical observations. To address this challenge, we introduce JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations. Language-conditioned task features guide a flow-matching policy, while masked attention restricts world prediction to instruction-independent dynamics history and supplied actions. In closed-loop evaluation on 40 trained LIBERO tasks, JEPA Dots achieves 84.9% overall success with approximately 39.1M parameters, compared with the published 78.7% of NanoVLA-S with 161.0M parameters under a different evaluation protocol. In the reference experiment, JEPA Dots also improves overall success from 76.0% for our task-ID-conditioned adaptation baseline to 84.9%, with LIBERO-Goal success increasing from 67.1% to 88.5%. Instruction-switching experiments further confirm that task representations and policy outputs respond to language changes, while dynamics representations and world predictions remain invariant under fixed observations and supplied actions.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: CoRA-VTLA: Contact-Guided Attention and Queryable Response Memory for Tactile Post-Training
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Chengye Song, Rui Song, Shengqi Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Hongzhou Wang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: CoRA-VTLA enhances pretrained vision-language-action models with tactile modules and memory retrieval, improving manipulation success rates by effectively integrating contact feedback.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: In precision manipulation, small errors in alignment or force can cause jamming or deformation, making contact feedback essential for adapting pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models to these tasks. A single tactile observation leaves the response to recent actions ambiguous. Direct tactile fusion during post-training can also disperse the action expert's visual attention and reduce the share it allocates to contact regions. To address these challenges, CoRA-VTLA augments pretrained VLAs with lightweight tactile modules. A queryable action-response memory retrieves recent contact responses so that the action expert can combine them with immediate tactile feedback. Contact-guided gaze supervision concentrates the visual attention of the tactile semantic token on image regions corresponding to fingertip contact. CoRA-VTLA achieves 73.33% mean success across three MuJoCo tasks, compared with 50% for direct tactile fusion with the same sensor inputs. It also achieves 67% success on an optical-tactile task from the public UniVTAC benchmark and 66.7% mean success across three real-robot tasks. These results show that tactile post-training helps pretrained VLAs adjust to changing contact.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: HOForce: Motion and Force Reconstruction of Hand-Object Interaction Using a Single-View RGB-D Video
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Jiahui Wang, Wanqing Du, Yuanbin Zou, Zhefeng Xu, Feng Xu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: HOForce effectively reconstructs hand-object interactions and interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video, improving motion tracking and accuracy in occluded scenarios.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Reconstructing hand-object interactions is an important task, and achieving it with a single camera makes large-scale capture practical but challenging due to heavy occlusions. We introduce HOForce to track hands and objects, and further recover interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video and known object properties. For two-hand manipulation, we jointly model fingertip forces of both hands and the contact forces between objects when two objects are presented. The reconstructed forces also improve motion tracking by giving pose constraints in the occluded regions. HOForce recovers hand and object motion more accurately on DexYCB and TACO and produces less hand-object penetration than interaction baselines on DexYCB. On our dataset of fingertip forces recorded with tactile sensors, HOForce reduces normal-force MAE by 24.5% relative to the strongest baseline. The recovered forces reproduce object motion in MuJoCo and transfer to other engines after adaptation.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Ying Wei, Defu Lian
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper examines how on-policy distillation alters ReAct interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and detrimental effects on performance.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

机器人控制实验室.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zhaolu Wang, Jiacheng Xu, Lihong Wang, Shuqing Wang, Jianjie Fang
机器人控制实验室.summary: HandWorldBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating hand-centric world models, highlighting the disparity between hand-pose control and effective object-state persistence across various embodiments.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, we introduce HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. To construct the benchmark, we develop a data curation pipeline that extracts hand-object interaction clips and screens them for quality, yielding 20,500 high-quality egocentric clips from over 600 hours of footage. We then manually select 500 clips covering seven task families for evaluation. Benchmarking eleven models under a unified protocol reveals that stronger hand-pose control does not consistently translate into coherent object-state evolution and persistence or robust cross-embodiment performance, with several specialized hand-control models underperforming general-purpose text/image-to-video generators on dexterous-hand tasks.

机器人控制实验室.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zihe Huang, Sirui Zhou, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Teng Ma
机器人控制实验室.summary: The F$^3$ framework enhances world-action models by optimizing experience utilization through Form, Fit, and Fusion, achieving significant performance improvements in robotic tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. We show that experience is valuable only in use: its value depends not on whether the source rollout succeeded but on what is stored, when it is used, and where it enters the policy. We therefore propose F$^3$, which makes these three decisions with Form, Fit, and Fusion. Form compresses successful and failed rollouts alike into short, verified operation records; Fit teaches the policy to read a record and to predict when it helps; Fusion injects the record's images, text and actions into the policy as a prefix and an action prior. Trained once on only 200 examples and deployed with a growing experience library, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on MolmoSpaces and RoboLab without any training on RoboLab: over native Cosmos 3 Nano, it raises success by 12.0 pp and 10.8 pp, reduces steps to success by 12.2% and 11.3%, and cuts regressions by 57%.

机器人控制实验室.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Rong Zou, Haiqing Hao, Davide Scaramuzza
机器人控制实验室.summary: ALIVE is an event-based method that efficiently updates visual foundation model features using events, significantly improving performance and reducing computational costs across various tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

机器人控制实验室.title: Rethinking Event-Based Object Detection through Representation-Level Temporal Aggregation and Model-Level Hypergraph Reasoning
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Meisen Wang, Hao Deng, Wei Bao, Chengjie Wang, Zhiqiang Tian
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces Ev-DTAD, an event-based object detection framework that enhances accuracy through hierarchical temporal aggregation and hypergraph reasoning, addressing limitations in existing methods.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Event cameras provide microsecond-level temporal resolution, low latency, and high dynamic range, offering potential for perception under fast motion and challenging illumination conditions. However, existing Event-based Object Detection (EOD) methods face limitations at both the representation and model levels: prior event representations usually encode temporal information indirectly through redundant structures, while detection models struggle to explicitly aggregate fragmented event responses into coherent high-order object features. To address these limitations, we present \textbf{Event Dual Temporal-Relational Aggregation Detector (Ev-DTAD)}, a unified EOD framework that integrates representation-level temporal encoding with model-level temporal-hypergraph reasoning. Specifically, we introduce \textbf{Hierarchical Temporal Aggregation (HTA)}, a compact three-channel pseudo-RGB representation that explicitly embeds temporal information across intra- and inter-window events. To further enhance detection under sparse and fragmented event responses, we propose \textbf{Frequency-aware Hypergraph Temporal Fusion (FHTF)}, which refines multi-scale event features through temporal evolution modeling and high-order relational reasoning. Extensive experiments on Gen1 (\textbf{+0.8 mAP}), 1Mpx/Gen4 (\textbf{+0.5 mAP}), and eTraM (\textbf{+3.0 mAP}) demonstrate that Ev-DTAD achieves a competitive accuracy--efficiency trade-off, validating the complementarity between compact temporal representation and temporal-hypergraph feature reasoning (Fig.~\ref{fig:bubble}). The code is available at: https://github.com/meisenwang/Ev-DTAD.

机器人控制实验室.title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng
机器人控制实验室.summary: Phoenix introduces a novel scene structure representation for world-action models, enhancing manipulation performance through dual-teacher distillation and causal aggregation of visual features.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

机器人控制实验室.title: Read Together, Answer Apart: How Earlier Questions Help Vision-Language Models Look
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Xinyi Guo, Kaile Huang, Xitong Ling, Mingyi He, Chende Zheng
机器人控制实验室.summary: The study reveals that co-asking enhances vision-language model accuracy by leveraging earlier questions to improve attention, while introducing a decoding mask further boosts performance.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are often asked several questions about the same image in a single prompt (co-asking), yet existing evaluations report conflicting accuracy gains and hallucinations at the prompt level without tracking how individual answers change. By pairing each question's single-question and co-asked answers across 22 open-weight VLMs (1B-35B), we find that erratic net shifts reflect two opposing effects: on Densely Captioned Images (DCI), every model repairs 15.4%-29.8% of its single-question errors under co-asking, while the share of correct answers turned wrong falls from 30.8% on weaker models to 4.7% on stronger ones. Across all 14 models supporting custom attention masks, we show through attention readouts and layer-window interventions that earlier same-image questions read visual information into their question tokens in the early-to-middle layers during prefill, helping later questions concentrate image attention onto their queried targets. This visual help accumulates across the scene even across non-overlapping regions, whereas blocking earlier questions from attending to the image lowers both target localization and accuracy in all 14 models. While cross-question help is established during shared question reading, part of the co-asking damage enters later during answer decoding when the decoder attends to other question stems. We therefore introduce Read Together, Answer Apart, a training-free decoding mask that keeps shared prefill intact and isolates each answer from other stems, improving co-asking accuracy on 12 of 14 models on DCI (up to +4.71 percentage points, closing 70% of the pooled gap to asking alone) and on 10, 8, and 5 of the 14 models on WebUI, FinTabNet, and GQA (up to +11.4, +5.3, and +1.1 points).

机器人控制实验室.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Shiwei Wu, Yuwen Pan, Zhi Li, Yaowen Li, Yan Zhou
机器人控制实验室.summary: AeroRSI is a framework that enables UAVs to iteratively learn from their navigation failures, improving success rates and reducing collisions without additional human input.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.

机器人控制实验室.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jiarui Guo, Saining Zhang, Jiaying Wan, Jiawei Weng, Junhao Chen
机器人控制实验室.summary: RFW-S is a comprehensive dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified deformable objects, enhancing robotic simulation with reliable physical properties and interaction behaviors across diverse categories.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

机器人控制实验室.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper proposes a wire protocol for detecting silent faults at the environment-trainer boundary in reinforcement learning, demonstrating effective fault identification through step ledgers and episode records.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Hongcheng Gao, Zelin Zheng, Alex Zhou, Jay Zhu, Shijia Ge
机器人控制实验室.summary: EmbodiedLab introduces a simulated laboratory for benchmarking embodied agents that must physically act to discover hidden properties, enhancing understanding through 35 quantitative experiments.

Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DLWM outperforms existing methods by 2-5 points in accuracy while reducing memory usage by 24%.

机器人控制实验室.title: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Xianhao Pan, Chi Li, Hanchao Li, Yunxin Liu, Jiankai Sun
机器人控制实验室.summary: JEPA Dots introduces a dual-latent framework for language-guided robot control, achieving 84.9% success by separating dynamics and task representations while maintaining invariant world predictions.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Predictive world models for language-guided robot control face a fundamental conditioning challenge: instructions should influence action selection without altering the predicted consequences of fixed actions under identical observations. To address this challenge, we introduce JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations. Language-conditioned task features guide a flow-matching policy, while masked attention restricts world prediction to instruction-independent dynamics history and supplied actions. In closed-loop evaluation on 40 trained LIBERO tasks, JEPA Dots achieves 84.9% overall success with approximately 39.1M parameters, compared with the published 78.7% of NanoVLA-S with 161.0M parameters under a different evaluation protocol. In the reference experiment, JEPA Dots also improves overall success from 76.0% for our task-ID-conditioned adaptation baseline to 84.9%, with LIBERO-Goal success increasing from 67.1% to 88.5%. Instruction-switching experiments further confirm that task representations and policy outputs respond to language changes, while dynamics representations and world predictions remain invariant under fixed observations and supplied actions.

机器人控制实验室.title: CoRA-VTLA: Contact-Guided Attention and Queryable Response Memory for Tactile Post-Training
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Chengye Song, Rui Song, Shengqi Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Hongzhou Wang
机器人控制实验室.summary: CoRA-VTLA enhances pretrained vision-language-action models with tactile modules and memory retrieval, improving manipulation success rates by effectively integrating contact feedback.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: In precision manipulation, small errors in alignment or force can cause jamming or deformation, making contact feedback essential for adapting pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models to these tasks. A single tactile observation leaves the response to recent actions ambiguous. Direct tactile fusion during post-training can also disperse the action expert's visual attention and reduce the share it allocates to contact regions. To address these challenges, CoRA-VTLA augments pretrained VLAs with lightweight tactile modules. A queryable action-response memory retrieves recent contact responses so that the action expert can combine them with immediate tactile feedback. Contact-guided gaze supervision concentrates the visual attention of the tactile semantic token on image regions corresponding to fingertip contact. CoRA-VTLA achieves 73.33% mean success across three MuJoCo tasks, compared with 50% for direct tactile fusion with the same sensor inputs. It also achieves 67% success on an optical-tactile task from the public UniVTAC benchmark and 66.7% mean success across three real-robot tasks. These results show that tactile post-training helps pretrained VLAs adjust to changing contact.

机器人控制实验室.title: HOForce: Motion and Force Reconstruction of Hand-Object Interaction Using a Single-View RGB-D Video
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jiahui Wang, Wanqing Du, Yuanbin Zou, Zhefeng Xu, Feng Xu
机器人控制实验室.summary: HOForce effectively reconstructs hand-object interactions and interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video, improving motion tracking and accuracy in occluded scenarios.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Reconstructing hand-object interactions is an important task, and achieving it with a single camera makes large-scale capture practical but challenging due to heavy occlusions. We introduce HOForce to track hands and objects, and further recover interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video and known object properties. For two-hand manipulation, we jointly model fingertip forces of both hands and the contact forces between objects when two objects are presented. The reconstructed forces also improve motion tracking by giving pose constraints in the occluded regions. HOForce recovers hand and object motion more accurately on DexYCB and TACO and produces less hand-object penetration than interaction baselines on DexYCB. On our dataset of fingertip forces recorded with tactile sensors, HOForce reduces normal-force MAE by 24.5% relative to the strongest baseline. The recovered forces reproduce object motion in MuJoCo and transfer to other engines after adaptation.

机器人控制实验室.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Ying Wei, Defu Lian
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper examines how on-policy distillation alters ReAct interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and detrimental effects on performance.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Zhaolu Wang, Jiacheng Xu, Lihong Wang, Shuqing Wang, Jianjie Fang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: HandWorldBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating hand-centric world models, highlighting the disparity between hand-pose control and effective object-state persistence across various embodiments.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, we introduce HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. To construct the benchmark, we develop a data curation pipeline that extracts hand-object interaction clips and screens them for quality, yielding 20,500 high-quality egocentric clips from over 600 hours of footage. We then manually select 500 clips covering seven task families for evaluation. Benchmarking eleven models under a unified protocol reveals that stronger hand-pose control does not consistently translate into coherent object-state evolution and persistence or robust cross-embodiment performance, with several specialized hand-control models underperforming general-purpose text/image-to-video generators on dexterous-hand tasks.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Zihe Huang, Sirui Zhou, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Teng Ma
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The F$^3$ framework enhances world-action models by optimizing experience utilization through Form, Fit, and Fusion, achieving significant performance improvements in robotic tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. What, then, makes good experience for a WAM? We show that experience is valuable only in use: its value depends not on whether the source rollout succeeded but on what is stored, when it is used, and where it enters the policy. We therefore propose F$^3$, which makes these three decisions with Form, Fit, and Fusion. Form compresses successful and failed rollouts alike into short, verified operation records; Fit teaches the policy to read a record and to predict when it helps; Fusion injects the record's images, text and actions into the policy as a prefix and an action prior. Trained once on only 200 examples and deployed with a growing experience library, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on MolmoSpaces and RoboLab without any training on RoboLab: over native Cosmos 3 Nano, it raises success by 12.0 pp and 10.8 pp, reduces steps to success by 12.2% and 11.3%, and cuts regressions by 57%.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Rong Zou, Haiqing Hao, Davide Scaramuzza
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: ALIVE is an event-based method that efficiently updates visual foundation model features using events, significantly improving performance and reducing computational costs across various tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Rethinking Event-Based Object Detection through Representation-Level Temporal Aggregation and Model-Level Hypergraph Reasoning
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Meisen Wang, Hao Deng, Wei Bao, Chengjie Wang, Zhiqiang Tian
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces Ev-DTAD, an event-based object detection framework that enhances accuracy through hierarchical temporal aggregation and hypergraph reasoning, addressing limitations in existing methods.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Event cameras provide microsecond-level temporal resolution, low latency, and high dynamic range, offering potential for perception under fast motion and challenging illumination conditions. However, existing Event-based Object Detection (EOD) methods face limitations at both the representation and model levels: prior event representations usually encode temporal information indirectly through redundant structures, while detection models struggle to explicitly aggregate fragmented event responses into coherent high-order object features. To address these limitations, we present \textbf{Event Dual Temporal-Relational Aggregation Detector (Ev-DTAD)}, a unified EOD framework that integrates representation-level temporal encoding with model-level temporal-hypergraph reasoning. Specifically, we introduce \textbf{Hierarchical Temporal Aggregation (HTA)}, a compact three-channel pseudo-RGB representation that explicitly embeds temporal information across intra- and inter-window events. To further enhance detection under sparse and fragmented event responses, we propose \textbf{Frequency-aware Hypergraph Temporal Fusion (FHTF)}, which refines multi-scale event features through temporal evolution modeling and high-order relational reasoning. Extensive experiments on Gen1 (\textbf{+0.8 mAP}), 1Mpx/Gen4 (\textbf{+0.5 mAP}), and eTraM (\textbf{+3.0 mAP}) demonstrate that Ev-DTAD achieves a competitive accuracy--efficiency trade-off, validating the complementarity between compact temporal representation and temporal-hypergraph feature reasoning (Fig.~\ref{fig:bubble}). The code is available at: https://github.com/meisenwang/Ev-DTAD.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: Phoenix introduces a novel scene structure representation for world-action models, enhancing manipulation performance through dual-teacher distillation and causal aggregation of visual features.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Read Together, Answer Apart: How Earlier Questions Help Vision-Language Models Look
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xinyi Guo, Kaile Huang, Xitong Ling, Mingyi He, Chende Zheng
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The study reveals that co-asking enhances vision-language model accuracy by leveraging earlier questions to improve attention, while introducing a decoding mask further boosts performance.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are often asked several questions about the same image in a single prompt (co-asking), yet existing evaluations report conflicting accuracy gains and hallucinations at the prompt level without tracking how individual answers change. By pairing each question's single-question and co-asked answers across 22 open-weight VLMs (1B-35B), we find that erratic net shifts reflect two opposing effects: on Densely Captioned Images (DCI), every model repairs 15.4%-29.8% of its single-question errors under co-asking, while the share of correct answers turned wrong falls from 30.8% on weaker models to 4.7% on stronger ones. Across all 14 models supporting custom attention masks, we show through attention readouts and layer-window interventions that earlier same-image questions read visual information into their question tokens in the early-to-middle layers during prefill, helping later questions concentrate image attention onto their queried targets. This visual help accumulates across the scene even across non-overlapping regions, whereas blocking earlier questions from attending to the image lowers both target localization and accuracy in all 14 models. While cross-question help is established during shared question reading, part of the co-asking damage enters later during answer decoding when the decoder attends to other question stems. We therefore introduce Read Together, Answer Apart, a training-free decoding mask that keeps shared prefill intact and isolates each answer from other stems, improving co-asking accuracy on 12 of 14 models on DCI (up to +4.71 percentage points, closing 70% of the pooled gap to asking alone) and on 10, 8, and 5 of the 14 models on WebUI, FinTabNet, and GQA (up to +11.4, +5.3, and +1.1 points).

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Shiwei Wu, Yuwen Pan, Zhi Li, Yaowen Li, Yan Zhou
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: AeroRSI is a framework that enables UAVs to iteratively learn from their navigation failures, improving success rates and reducing collisions without additional human input.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jiarui Guo, Saining Zhang, Jiaying Wan, Jiawei Weng, Junhao Chen
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: RFW-S is a comprehensive dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified deformable objects, enhancing robotic simulation with reliable physical properties and interaction behaviors across diverse categories.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper proposes a wire protocol for detecting silent faults at the environment-trainer boundary in reinforcement learning, demonstrating effective fault identification through step ledgers and episode records.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: EmbodiedLab: Beyond Manipulation, Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Hongcheng Gao, Zelin Zheng, Alex Zhou, Jay Zhu, Shijia Ge
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: EmbodiedLab introduces a simulated laboratory for benchmarking embodied agents that must physically act to discover hidden properties, enhancing understanding through 35 quantitative experiments.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Physical action not only changes the state of an environment but is also the way to know its hidden properties: what cannot be seen must be inferred from the feedback to the change. As embodied agents advance from executing procedures to pursuing goals, success depends on properties neither given nor visible, so they must act to know. Existing benchmarks separate changing from knowing: manipulation benchmarks give the target state, so nothing has to be found out, whereas exploration and discovery benchmarks let the agent find out by looking or querying, so nothing physical has to be changed. Quantitative science experiments offer a natural testbed: the properties sought are new in every instance, appear only in instrument readings under conditions the agent sets up, and can be checked exactly. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a simulated laboratory of 35 such experiments. Given only a goal, the agent must decide what to measure, operate the apparatus with a robot arm, read instruments through cameras and judge when its readings suffice. Its 30 determination tasks specify what to find out, whereas its 5 optimization tasks ask only for the best result the apparatus allows. With native control, the strongest of seven frontier agents succeeds on 41.4% of the tasks. Ablations reveal two bottlenecks: contact-rich manipulation, where ground-truth depth and motion planning change the success rate by at most 10 points, whereas executing every operation for the agent on five of the tasks raises it from at most 20% to at least 70%, so what an agent can know is bounded by how reliably it acts; and closed-loop experimental rigor, where with manipulation supplied, agents fail to gather sufficient readings or read instruments accurately, and most optimization runs stop at one design. Beyond evaluation, EmbodiedLab offers a resamplable environment with verifiable rewards for training embodied agents.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Autonomous Video Generation for Self-Evolving World Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xin Wang, Wenxuan Liu, Tongtong Feng, Wenwu Zhu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: This paper introduces autonomous video generation for self-evolving world models, emphasizing counterfactual controllability and closed-loop optimization to enhance actionable predictions for embodied agents.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Large-scale video generation models are increasingly described as world models because they can learn rich spatiotemporal regularities from visual data. We argue that an ideal world model should benefit in a self-evolving generative character. As such, a self-evolving world model can be realized via a generative model conditioned by various constraints, whose future predictions are refined through feedback. However, traditional visually plausible predictions alone are not enough to establish whether an imagined future is physically actionable for a particular embodied agent, failing to provide informative feedback from environments for self-evolving improvement. To realize self-evolving world models, this article proposes the concept of autonomous video generation, which is evaluated through counterfactual controllability, i.e., the ability to i) generate intervention-conditioned futures, ii) bind these future frames to embodiment constraints, iii) verify them under distribution shifts, and iv) distil surviving branches into compact variables for decision-making. We formalize a four-stage closed-loop optimization of Generation, Binding, Verification and Distillation, together with four corresponding evaluation metrics: novelty, consistency, out-of-distribution (OOD) and efficiency. We further discuss two examples, i.e., drones and manipulators, as early embodied testbeds where wind, sensing limits, actuation delay, contact dynamics and recovery constraints can be systematically perturbed and verified. The central claim is that the framework of autonomous video generation for self-evolving world models should not be judged by video fidelity alone, but by whether the generated frames improve valid action under counterfactual interventions and various embodiment constraints.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: DLWM: Diverse Latent World Models for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: DLWM introduces a multimodal reasoning framework that utilizes diverse latent hypotheses and adaptive reinforcement learning to enhance accuracy and reduce memory usage in complex reasoning tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have improved considerably in recent years. A uniform reasoning strategy not only limits the model's ability to explore multiple hypotheses but also incurs high memory usage and rollout cost. We present DLWM (Diverse Latent World Models), a multimodal reasoning framework that combines latent-space reasoning with reinforcement learning. First, we construct a set of diverse latent world hypotheses in continuous latent space, each representing a candidate interpretation of the visual input, and unfold latent reasoning independently on each hypothesis. An orthogonality-based diversity regularizer discourages hypothesis collapse. Second, we formulate the latent reasoning process as a resource-constrained sequential decision problem and introduce a resource-aware reinforcement learning policy that adaptively allocates computation across hypotheses, dynamically deciding whether to expand a reasoning path, prune a hypothesis, merge reasoning paths, or produce the final answer, thereby substantially reducing memory footprint and improving rollout efficiency. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DLWM outperforms existing methods by 2-5 points in accuracy while reducing memory usage by 24%.
